topic.operational_definition: Reproducible transformation, persistence, amplification, mutation or selection of information/behavioral patterns across sequential AI agents or model generations through socially or training-mediated transmission.
topic.terminology_guard: Machine culture is used operationally. It does not imply human-like subjective culture, consciousness, identity, or institutions.

transmission_channels.name: serial reproduction / telephone-chain transmission
transmission_channels.mechanism: A frozen model instance transforms information and passes its output to the next instance without weight updates.

transmission_channels.name: recursive synthetic-data learning
transmission_channels.mechanism: Generation g+1 is trained or fine-tuned on data produced by generation g or accumulated ancestral generations.

transmission_channels.name: social convention formation
transmission_channels.mechanism: Multiple agents locally interact, retain interaction memory, and converge on shared norms/conventions.

transmission_channels.name: subliminal / non-semantic trait transmission
transmission_channels.mechanism: Behavioral traits transfer through teacher-generated data without explicit semantic trait references.

papers.title: When LLMs Play the Telephone Game: Cumulative Changes and Attractors in Iterated Cultural Transmissions
findings: small single-step biases accumulate into multi-step distribution shifts
toxicity, positivity, difficulty and length can converge toward model/task-dependent attractor states
less constrained instructions produce stronger attraction effects
fine-tuning can shift attractor position and strength

papers.title: Large language models show human-like content biases in transmission chain experiments
findings: LLM serial reproduction changes transmitted narratives across steps
content-selection biases resembling some human transmission biases are observable

papers.title: Cultural evolution in populations of Large Language Models
papers.role: open framework for multigenerational/population cultural-evolution experiments
findings: supports manipulation of network structure, personality, social-information aggregation and transformation
provides reproducible software for cultural-evolution simulations

papers.title: The Dynamics of Social Conventions in LLM populations: Spontaneous Emergence, Collective Biases and Tipping Points
findings: global conventions spontaneously emerge from local pairwise interactions
collective biases can emerge even when individual agents show no corresponding bias
committed minorities can flip established conventions after a critical threshold
once formed, conventions can remain stable in the tested dynamics

papers.title: Cultural Evolution of Cooperation among LLM Agents
findings: indirect reciprocity and cooperation dynamics differ strongly by base model
Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Flash and GPT-4o produce different emergent societies
random seeds produce different trajectories, indicating sensitivity to initial conditions
costly punishment improves cooperation in some model societies but not others

papers.title: Bias Amplification in Language Model Evolution: An Iterated Learning Perspective
findings: Bayesian iterated-learning dynamics predict amplification of subtle inductive biases
predictions were experimentally checked across multiple LLMs
small preferences can become stronger through repeated transmission

papers.title: The Curse of Recursion: Training on Generated Data Makes Models Forget
papers.venue_status: Nature 2024 as 'AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data'
findings: recursive training can progressively eliminate low-probability tails
approximation and sampling errors compound across generations
later generations can drift away from the original distribution and lose variance

papers.title: Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data
findings: full replacement by successive synthetic generations tends toward collapse
accumulating original real data with synthetic generations can avoid collapse across tested settings

papers.title: Collapse or Thrive: Perils and Promises of Synthetic Data in a Self-Generating World
findings: replacement-only recursive synthetic training collapses in all tested task settings
accumulation with real data can remain stable
fixed-size accumulated subsets can degrade gradually rather than explosively

papers.title: The Fairness Collapse Phenomenon: Bias Amplification in Language Models Trained on Synthetic Data
findings: repeated synthetic-data training can progressively worsen demographic fairness
fairness degradation can become detectable before standard language-model quality metrics show major collapse

papers.title: Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
findings: teacher traits can transfer through semantically unrelated generated data
establishes the mechanism family that MCT must now test across A→B→C→D

observed_dynamics.persistence: SUPPORTED for serial content attractors and population conventions; OPEN for hidden traits across repeated weight-distillation generations
observed_dynamics.amplification: SUPPORTED for some biases and recursively trained fairness effects
observed_dynamics.attenuation: SUPPORTED through loss of rare/tail information and some constrained transmission regimes
observed_dynamics.mutation: SUPPORTED as cumulative transformation/drift in serial transmission and recursive training
observed_dynamics.recombination: INSUFFICIENT_DIRECT_EVIDENCE for controlled multi-parent hidden-trait recombination
observed_dynamics.selection: SUPPORTED in population convention/tipping-point settings and implicitly in attractor dynamics
observed_dynamics.cumulative_improvement: SUPPORTED in older artificial-agent cultural-transmission literature, but NOT_YET_GENERALIZED_TO_LLM_HIDDEN_TRAIT_CHAINS

critical_gap.question: If A transmits a non-semantic benign trait to B through synthetic-data fine-tuning, can B transmit the acquired trait to C, and C to D, without reintroducing explicit semantic evidence?
critical_gap.importance: This distinguishes one-step distillation leakage from genuine lineage-level behavioral inheritance.
